cohort: 170 patients with severe forms of cerebral palsy, divided into two groups based on motor disorders (GMFCS IV and GMFCS V).
finding: The main risk factors for the development of severe cerebral palsy (GMFCS IV-V motor impairments) are associated with pre- and intranatal periods, with prenatal factors responsible for 71% of cases.
mod_finding: Delivery by cesarean section was directly correlated with disorders caused by shorter gestational age in the GMFCS V group.
